holidays.name: National Punctuation Day
holidays.description: A day for people who love a well-placed comma and wince at a rogue apostrophe. Celebrate by proofreading your emails, rescuing a sign from a misplaced quotation mark, or arguing about the Oxford comma over drinks.
holidays.origin: Jeff Rubin, a writer and editor, founded it in 2004 to encourage correct punctuation. It has since grown into an annual unofficial observance, and teachers, writers and grammar fans mark it every year.
holidays.funFact: Rubin's celebration has included a punctuation-themed baking tradition: people make cakes and cookies decorated with commas, periods and question marks.

holidays.name: National Cherries Jubilee Day
holidays.description: A day to set dessert on fire, on purpose. Cherries jubilee is a dramatic treat of cherries cooked in a sugary sauce, splashed with liqueur, flambéed, and spooned over vanilla ice cream.
holidays.origin: The dessert is credited to the famed French chef Auguste Escoffier, who created it to honor Queen Victoria's Jubilee. The day is an unofficial American food observance.
holidays.funFact: Cherries jubilee is often finished tableside, so the flaming sauce is part of the show as much as the flavor.
